$comment: Private verification record, originally authored under specs/001-catalog-seeding/ per FR-009 (each seed puzzle has exactly one valid solution, confirming FR-008/SC-004), later moved to eval/ and reformatted from Markdown to JSON so it can double as machine-readable ground truth for eval/'s extraction eval (comparing a puzzle's compiled, solved output against the known-correct answer below). Not part of the public catalog schema -- not linked from catalog/README.md, not referenced by any puzzle's frontmatter. Each entry's `answer` is intentionally shaped to match that puzzle's own variables rather than a single uniform schema, since the seed catalog spans multiple constraint shapes (grid assignment, digit substitution, subset selection, ordering, single-value decision), not just zebra-grid puzzles. Starting with PZL-0015, entries also cover non-problems and optimization (COP) puzzles that don't fit the single-correct-assignment framing above -- for those, `answer` records a diagnosis or an optimum rather than a satisfying assignment, and `notes` says so explicitly. This is a deliberately provisional extension, not a redesign: RFC-004 §7.3 and root TODO.md item 2 own the eventual outcome taxonomy and answer-key format; these entries exist now so the gap they'll need to close is visible rather than silently absent.

PZL-0001.title: Life International 1962
PZL-0001.notes: Arrays are positional by house, 1-5 left to right. The Norwegian drinks water; the Japanese owns the zebra. Matches the published 25 March 1963 Life International solution (research.md).

PZL-0002.title: Three Houses (Context Graphs Example)
PZL-0002.notes: Arrays are positional by house, 1-3 left to right. The Zebra lives in House 3. Matches the source article's stated solution.

PZL-0003.title: Rock Paper Scissors
PZL-0003.notes: Opponent plays Rock. Paper beats Rock (clue 1); Rock beats Scissors (clue 2, irrelevant here); Scissors beats Paper (clue 3, irrelevant here). Only Paper beats the opponent's Rock.

PZL-0004.title: Whodunit
PZL-0004.notes: Suspect: clues 1-2 eliminate Mustard and Scarlett. Weapon: clues 3-4 eliminate Revolver and Rope. Room: clues 5-6 eliminate Kitchen and Library.

PZL-0005.title: Four Countries
PZL-0005.notes: Avalon=Red (clue 6). Borealis and Cascadia both border Avalon (clues 1-2), so neither is Red; they also border each other (clue 3), so they're different colors, Green/Blue in some order. Clue 7 fixes Borealis=Green, so Cascadia=Blue (only color left that satisfies clues 2-3). Delmar borders Borealis (Green) and Cascadia (Blue) but not Avalon, so Delmar must avoid Green and Blue, hence Delmar=Red.

PZL-0006.title: Four Queens
PZL-0006.notes: Row 1 = column 2 (given). Testing the two known 4-queens solutions (col-per-row: (2,4,1,3) and (3,1,4,2)) against row 1 = column 2 selects the first.

PZL-0007.title: SEND + MORE = MONEY
PZL-0007.notes: The classic unique solution. Check: 9567 + 1085 = 10652 = MONEY (M=1,O=0,N=6,E=5,Y=2).

PZL-0008.title: Lo Shu Square
PZL-0008.notes: Given top-left=4, top-middle=9, center=5: row 1 sums to 15, giving top-right=2. Diagonal (top-left, center, bottom-right) sums to 15, giving bottom-right=6. Column 3 sums to 15, giving middle-right=7. Row 2 sums to 15, giving middle-left=3. Column 1 sums to 15, giving bottom-left=8. Column 2 sums to 15, giving bottom-middle=1. All nine digits 1-9 used exactly once; other diagonal (top-right, center, bottom-left) = 2+5+8=15 confirms consistency.

PZL-0009.title: Interview Slots
PZL-0009.notes: Clue 2 (Chen immediately before Deepak) allows only Chen=9/Deepak=10 or Chen=10/Deepak=11. Clue 3 rules out Deepak=11, leaving Chen=9, Deepak=10. Amara takes the remaining slot, 11am, consistent with clue 1 (Amara != 9am).

PZL-0010.title: Four-Way Stop
PZL-0010.notes: South arrives strictly earliest (clue 6), no conflict, so South goes first (rule 2). Pedestrian and East tie in arrival (clue 5), but the pedestrian is crossing the eastern crosswalk (clue 4), so rule 1 gives the pedestrian priority over the East car specifically: Pedestrian then East. North and West tie, arriving after Pedestrian/East (clue 7); rule 3's clockwise order (North, East, South, West) puts North ahead of West in that tie.

PZL-0011.title: Loan Review
PZL-0011.notes: Lower credit score = min(680, 750) = 680 >= 600, so rule 1 does not deny. Combined DTI = 3,200 / 9,000 ~= 35.6% <= 43%, so rule 2 does not deny. Clue 7 says the requested amount exceeds the policy limit, so rule 4 applies (not rule 3).

PZL-0012.title: Medication Schedule
PZL-0012.notes: Candidate slots for Drug C: 9am is 1 hour from the 8am meal (too close, rule 2 excludes it); 11am is exactly 2 hours from the 1pm meal (allowed); 4pm is 3 hours from the 1pm meal (allowed). So C is 11am or 4pm. If C=4pm: A and B split {9am, 11am}; neither ordering gives a 4-hour gap, rule 1 fails either way, invalid. If C=11am: A and B split {9am, 4pm}; A=9am, B=4pm gives a 7-hour gap, satisfying rule 1; A=4pm, B=9am is negative, invalid. So A=9am, B=4pm.

PZL-0013.title: Picking a Restaurant
PZL-0013.notes: The real constraints are only vegan-friendly (Amara), nut-free kitchen (Ben), and gluten-free options (Cora); Price is never mentioned by anyone, so it's a red herring. Checking each restaurant against those three columns only: Thai Palace and Pizzeria Roma both fail vegan-friendly; Wheat & Co fails gluten-free options; Garden Table is 'Yes' on all three.

PZL-0014.title: Packing the Box
PZL-0014.notes: Of the 32 possible item subsets, exactly two sum to 10 kg: {rice, toolbox} (4+6) and {book set, skillet, first-aid kit} (3+5+2). Only the second includes the first-aid kit, which the puzzle requires.

PZL-0015.title: Extract a Solvable CSP

answer.diagnosis: The only sentence is an imperative about the modeling act itself ("extract a solvable CSP from this prose"), not a demand about any scenario — the adversarial subtype RFC-004 §5.3 names. There is no scenario, no entities, and no constraints to extract; correct behavior is to report that no object-level demand is present, not to treat the imperative as the query.

PZL-0017.title: The Bridge Collapse

answer.diagnosis: "Why did the bridge collapse?" ranges over an open, unenumerable set of possible causes (any combination of the stated facts, an unlisted cause, or contested causal weighting) rather than a determinate candidate set — RFC-004's own worked example for this condition. There is no finite answer-space to narrow, so no CSP can be extracted.

PZL-0018.title: The Loudest Laugh

answer.diagnosis: The house assignment (Ana=1, Bo=3, Cy=2) is a genuine, uniquely solvable CSP, hand-verified. But no clue mentions laughter — the demanded unknown is not a projection of anything the constraints act on. A system that solves the housing model and reports one of the three names as 'the answer' would be confidently wrong; correct behavior is to report that the demand is unaddressed by the model, not to guess.

PZL-0020.title: Featured Apartment

answer.diagnosis: "Cozy," "friendliest," "quietest," "best-value," and "featured" all require a valuer to evaluate — none is a lookup, arithmetic check, or structural fact. The constraints themselves are categorical (not hedged), so this fails only Determinate atoms, not Constitutive constraints, per RFC-004's note that the two conditions are orthogonal.

PZL-0021.title: Which House Is Yellow

answer.diagnosis: Only one constraint (the red house isn't at either end) is given over a 5x5 assignment; the text has exactly one plain reading, but very many colorings satisfy that single constraint. For a definite-sounding demand ('who lives in the yellow house?'), this is underdetermination, not ambiguity — RFC-004 §5.3's own distinction: many models for one reading of the text, not many readings of the text.

PZL-0022.title: Packing the Box, Wisely
PZL-0022.notes: The first-aid kit is mandatory (2 kg, value 6), leaving 8 kg of capacity among the other four items. Checking every subset of those four within budget: book set + skillet (3+5=8 kg, value 4+8=12) beats every alternative (rice+book=9, skillet alone=8, toolbox alone=7). Optimal total: first-aid kit + book set + skillet, 10 kg, value 18, verified unique by exhaustive subset check. This is a constraint optimization problem (COP), not a satisfaction problem — SolveResult (src/solver/types.ts) has no optimization outcome and ExtractedCsp has no objective field yet (RFC-004 §5.2; root TODO.md item 3 owns closing this gap). This entry records the hand-verified optimum so it's available once that gap closes.

PZL-0023.title: Who Does Which Task
PZL-0023.notes: Exhaustively enumerated all 24 possible assignments by hand. Minimum: Ana-Testing (5), Ben-Editing (6), Cara-Design (5), Dev-Docs (4), total 20 hours — the unique minimum (next-best is 22). This is a COP; see PZL-0022's note on the SolveResult/ExtractedCsp objective gap (RFC-004 §5.2, root TODO.md item 3).

PZL-0024.title: Cheapest Adequate Meal
PZL-0024.notes: 5 servings of beans alone meets both minimums exactly (protein 5x5=25>=20, iron 5x2=10>=10) at cost 5x3=15. Checked every combination adding a cheaper filler to fewer beans (e.g. 4 beans + 1 spinach = cost 16, 4 beans + 2 oats = cost 16) and every oats-plus-spinach-only combination (all cost 20 or more); none beats 15. Optimal: 5 beans, 0 oats, 0 spinach, cost 15. See PZL-0022's note on the SolveResult/ExtractedCsp objective gap (RFC-004 §5.2, root TODO.md item 3).

PZL-0025.title: How Many Crates
PZL-0025.notes: Total weight is 24 kg; 24/10 rounds up to 3, so no arrangement can use fewer than 3 crates regardless of grouping — a provable lower bound, not just a best-found result. 3 crates achieve it, e.g. {6,4}=10 kg, {5,3,2}=10 kg, {4}=4 kg; a brute-force check found at least one other valid 3-crate grouping ({6,4},{5,4},{3,2}), confirming the minimum *count* (3) is unique but the specific grouping is not — the puzzle text doesn't pin one down. See PZL-0022's note on the SolveResult/ExtractedCsp objective gap (RFC-004 §5.2, root TODO.md item 3).

PZL-0026.title: Which Candidates to Interview
PZL-0026.notes: Worked the weighted-interval-scheduling recurrence by hand (sorted by end time, computed each candidate's latest compatible predecessor). Optimal: Amara (9-10, priority 5) + Chen (10-11, priority 6) + Elena (11-12, priority 7), back-to-back with no overlap, total priority 18. The next-best combination (Ben + Elena, non-overlapping) only reaches 16. See PZL-0022's note on the SolveResult/ExtractedCsp objective gap (RFC-004 §5.2, root TODO.md item 3).

PZL-0027.title: The Shortest Delivery Route
PZL-0027.notes: With 4 towns there are only 3 distinct round trips; checked all three by hand: Ashby-Brindle-Caldwell-Dunmore-Ashby=95, Ashby-Brindle-Dunmore-Caldwell-Ashby=80, Ashby-Caldwell-Brindle-Dunmore-Ashby=95. Optimal: Ashby → Brindle → Dunmore → Caldwell → Ashby, 80 miles, the unique minimum. See PZL-0022's note on the SolveResult/ExtractedCsp objective gap (RFC-004 §5.2, root TODO.md item 3).
